paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Job is hurting, and he takes it straight to God. He doesn't hide, and he doesn't put on a show. He asks, "How many are my iniquities and sins?" and he asks why God seems to treat him "as Your enemy" (Job 13:23-24). Job believes God is the One to bring it to, and that matters for every baker who has ever had a hard question.

Now look at how honest Job gets about life. He says man "is short of days and full of trouble" (Job 14:1). He sees a cut-down tree sprout again, and then he asks, "When a man dies, will he live again?" (Job 14:14). I think that question is the ache of the whole passage. Job doesn't have the answer yet, and the Bible lets him ask it out loud. So you can ask your own big questions too, even the heavy ones.

Then Job does something that makes my mustache tingle. He says, "All the days of my hard service I will wait, until my renewal comes" (Job 14:14). He pictures a day when God calls and he answers, because God will "desire the work of Your hands" (Job 14:15). I know a little about waiting in the dark, and about a God who reaches in when you think you're forgotten. Job's story isn't over, and neither is this conversation, so keep waiting and keep talking to God, baker.
